# Jubilees Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Sarah's Death; Isaac Married; Abraham's Instructions; Rebecca and Jacob

---

**19:1** And in the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee, Abraham returned and dwelt opposite Hebron, that is Kirjath Arba, two weeks of years.

**19:2** And in the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of the life of Sarah were accomplished, and she died in Hebron.

**19:3** And Abraham went to mourn over her and bury her, and we tried him [to see] whether his spirit was patient and he was not distressed at the loss of her; and he was found patient in this, and was not disturbed; for in patience of spirit he conversed with the children of Heth, to the intent that they should give him a place in which to bury his dead.

**19:4** And the LORD gave him grace before all who saw him, and he besought in gentleness the sons of Heth; and they gave him the land of the double cave over against Mamre, that is the field of Ephron, which is of the sons of Heth; and they confirmed to him the land and the cave which is in it as a possession for ever before all the sons of Heth who dwelt in Hebron.

**19:5** And these things were written in the book which was in Hebron.

**19:6** And Abraham buried Sarah in the double cave, which is in Mamre, that is Hebron.

**19:7** And in the fourth year of this week he took a wife for his son Isaac, and her name was Rebecca, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, the brother of Abraham, the sister of Laban.

**19:8** And she became his wife, and Isaac was pleased with her, and was comforted from the mourning for Sarah his mother.

**19:9** And it came to pass in the second year of the forty-second jubilee, in the first week, that Abraham took for himself a wife, whose name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.

**19:10** And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, six sons; and the sons of Jokshan were Sheba and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan were Raguel and Nabaoth; and the sons of Midian were Ephah and Epher and Hanoch and Abida and Eldaah; and all these were Keturah's sons.

**19:11** And Abraham gave gifts to the sons of Keturah and sent them away from Isaac his son towards the east and away from him.

**19:12** And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac his son, and to the sons of Ishmael he gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac; and Isaac was above all in his father's affections.

**19:13** And Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, went together and dwelt from Pharan to the entering in of Babylon, in all the land to the east, facing the desert.

**19:14** And these mingled with one another, and their name was called Arabs, and Ishmaelites.

**19:15** And in the twenty-fifth year of this jubilee, when Abraham had grown old and his eyes were dim, and the days of his life were drawing near to an end, Isaac called his son Esau and said unto him: "Go into the field and hunt game for me, and make me savory meat, that I may eat and bless thee."

**19:16** Abraham called his grandson Jacob, for Rebekah had given birth to two sons, Esau and Jacob, and Jacob was a smooth man, and Esau was a rough man and hairy.

**19:17** And Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.

**19:18** And Abraham saw that the deeds of Esau were evil, and that all his ways were perverse; for Esau was not right and upright in the ways of God.

**19:19** And he called his grandson Jacob and said to him: "Jacob, my son!" And he said: "Here am I, grandfather." And he kissed him and blessed him.

**19:20** And he said: "Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan; take a wife from the family of my father, from his seed; take a wife from the house of my father."

**19:21** "And the Most High God will bless thee, the God of Abraham thy father, and he will increase and multiply thee, and thou wilt become an assembly of nations."

**19:22** "And he will give to thee and to thy seed the land of thy sojourning — the land of my father — and thou shalt possess it and dwell in it for ever."

**19:23** And he called his son Isaac and gave him commandments, saying to him: "I am growing old, and I do not know the day of my death, and I am full of days."

**19:24** "Behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old today, and throughout all the days of my life I have remembered the LORD, and sought with all my heart to do his will and to walk uprightly in all his ways."

**19:25** "My soul hated idols, and I have despised those who served them; I have given my heart and spirit that I should observe to do the will of him who created me."

**19:26** "For he is the living God; he is holy and faithful, he is righteous beyond all, and there is with him no accepting of persons and no receiving of gifts; for God is righteous, and executeth judgment on all those who transgress his commandments and despise his covenant."

**19:27** And now I command thee, my son Isaac: Walk uprightly before him and serve him in truth and righteousness and love him with all thy heart and with all thy soul.

**19:28** Circumcise every male in thy house; and observe to keep the covenant of God which thou didst enter into with him; and keep his statutes which he commanded Abraham thy father.

**19:29** Love truth and righteousness, and hate iniquity and transgression, and keep thyself from all pollution; and eat not any blood.

**19:30** And in this feast he went to Abraham his father, and Abraham loved Jacob greatly above all his sons; and he gave him the blessing of the first-born, and spoke to him regarding what befits the first-born.

---
*EMET notes: Isaac's narrative (v.15) conflates with Abraham calling Jacob (v.16) — a textual complexity. Abraham's final testimony (vv.23-29) is a farewell address emphasizing monotheism, righteousness, and circumcision. The blessing of the first-born transferred to Jacob (v.30) anticipates the Jacob-Esau conflict.*
